chunks: About a man whose head nods off while he is in salat (prayer), standing or bowing, he said: “There is no wudu (ablution) upon him.”

key_terms.رَأْسَهُ: his head, indicating physical nodding from drowsiness
key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification required for prayer

ai.seo_question: Does briefly nodding off during salat (prayer) invalidate wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about slight drowsiness during salat (prayer). It indicates that nodding off briefly while standing or in ruku' does not invalidate wudu (ablution).

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Sama'a ibn Mehran asked him about a man who nods off while standing or bowing in prayer.
Imam (as) said: 'He does not need to perform ablution.'.
